title: protect.js poll cadence: the first two sleeps after the immediate sweep are 15s regardless of pending jobs, then 30s or 5 minutes by pending count
answers: Why does the Protect check now recheck after 15 seconds even when only a few jobs are pending?
Where is the polling interval for the Protect workflow chosen, and how many sleeps are short?
Why did the fast 5-second polling for PRs with five or fewer pending jobs disappear?
Protect check is slow to fail or pass on a busy PR; what controls how often it re-polls?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/protect.js:getSleepLength is the sleep-interval chooser for the Protect check-polling loop in the Copilot/CI protect workflow; it takes the loop's iterationCount and the number of pending jobs and returns the milliseconds to wait before the next fetchChecks sweep.
Rule: in getSleepLength, return 15 * 1000 whenever iterationCount <= 2, independent of numPendingJobs; for later iterations keep the existing (numPendingJobs <= 7 ? 30 : 5 * 60) * 1000 choice. The earlier shortcut that gave 5s only when both iterationCount <= 5 and numPendingJobs <= 5 is removed, so the pending-job count no longer shortens the early cadence.
Constraints: this sets the cadence only; it does not change pass/fail logic or what fetchChecks reads. Each sweep can make several paginated GitHub API calls (workflow runs plus jobs per run), and a review on this PR flagged that the 15s early polls add API pressure on busy PRs and raise rate-limit exhaustion risk; that trade-off was accepted for earlier failure detection. A review comment also said the code polls every 10s for three sweeps, which does not match this diff or the PR description (15s, two polls); treat the diff as the source of truth and verify before changing either the code or the description. Applies only to protect.js polling, not to other workflows' retry timing.
applies: Any change to how the Protect check-polling script in .github/workflows waits between sweeps, or to how many early sweeps happen before the 30s/5min backoff.
says: Pull request protection checks take too long to detect early test suite failures.
Why did the fast initial five second polling on pull requests change to fifteen?
Status check polling causes high API usage on pull requests with many pending jobs.
Adjust how frequently the protection workflow rechecks pending pull request job statuses.
search: In .github/workflows/protect.js:getSleepLength, the check-polling loop sets the first two sleep intervals (iterationCount <= 2) to 15 seconds regardless of numPendingJobs, before backing off to 30 seconds (if numPendingJobs <= 7) or 5 minutes. This eliminates the previous 5-second polling shortcut that applied when iterationCount <= 5 and numPendingJobs <= 5, trading increased GitHub API pressure and rate-limit risk for faster failure detection. This guidance sets the cadence only and does not alter fetchChecks queries or pass/fail gating logic.
